laws.title: Hands-Free Driving Law
laws.subtitle: MI Code §Traffic Code — No handheld devices while driving
laws.fullDescription: Michigan prohibits holding or using handheld electronic devices while driving. Handheld device ban while driving.
laws.exceptions: Emergency 911 calls are exempt from hands-free requirements.

quiz.q: Is handheld phone use banned while driving in Michigan?
quiz.explanation: Michigan: handheld device use while driving is prohibited.

laws.title: Non-Resident Hunting & Fishing License
laws.subtitle: MCL §Fish & Game Code — Non-residents must purchase licenses
laws.fullDescription: Non-residents must obtain a valid Michigan hunting or fishing license before taking game or fish. Annual non-resident fishing licenses cost approximately $45; hunting licenses cost approximately $150. Some species require additional tags.
laws.penalty: Class A misdemeanor or felony; fines up to $1000 plus equipment forfeiture.
laws.exceptions: Residents are exempt from non-resident fees.

quiz.q: What is the penalty for hunting without a license in Michigan?

laws.title: Impaired Driving (DUI/DWI)
laws.subtitle: MCL §Vehicle Code — 0.08% BAC limit
laws.fullDescription: Michigan prohibits operating a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher. Commercial drivers: 0.04%. Drivers under 21: 0.02 BAC. Implied consent laws apply.
laws.penalty: First offense: $500–$1,000 fine, license suspension, up to 1 year jail. Subsequent offenses carry mandatory minimums and longer suspensions.
laws.exceptions: None — even prescription medication impairment can result in DUI charges.

quiz.q: What BAC triggers a DUI in Michigan for regular drivers?
quiz.explanation: The legal BAC limit in Michigan is 0.08% for regular drivers, consistent with all US states.

laws.title: Open Container Law
laws.subtitle: MCL §Vehicle Code — No open alcohol in vehicles
laws.fullDescription: Michigan prohibits open alcoholic beverage containers in the passenger area of motor vehicles on public roads. Open container law applies to driver and passengers.
laws.penalty: $250 fine; applies to driver and passengers.
laws.exceptions: Passengers in for-hire vehicles (taxis, limos) may be exempt.

quiz.q: Can passengers drink alcohol in a private car in Michigan?
quiz.explanation: Michigan's open container law applies to all vehicle occupants.

laws.title: Recreational Cannabis — Legal

laws.exceptions: Medical patients exempt.

quiz.q: Is recreational cannabis legal in Michigan?
quiz.explanation: Michigan legalized recreational cannabis in 2018.

laws.title: Medical Cannabis — Legal
laws.subtitle: MCL §Health Code — Medical cannabis program
laws.fullDescription: Michigan has a medical cannabis program.

laws.exceptions: Registered patients are exempt from possession penalties.

quiz.q: Does Michigan have a medical cannabis program?
quiz.explanation: Michigan has a medical cannabis program.

laws.title: Firearm Carry Law — Shall-issue

laws.exceptions: Firearms prohibited in schools, courts, and government buildings.

laws.title: Stand Your Ground / Castle Doctrine

laws.title: Minimum Wage Law

laws.fullDescription: Michigan follows at-will employment. Employers may terminate for any legal reason; employees may quit anytime. at-will employment with standard exceptions.

laws.penalty: Violation of DV protective order: misdemeanor to felony..
laws.exceptions: Mutual protective orders may be issued in some circumstances.

quiz.q: Does Michigan have mandatory arrest policies for domestic violence?
quiz.explanation: Michigan: DV protective orders and protections available.

laws.title: Stalking & Cyberstalking Laws
laws.subtitle: MCL §Criminal Code — Stalking prohibition
laws.fullDescription: Michigan prohibits stalking — repeated non-consensual contact causing substantial distress. Stalking prohibited; cyberstalking covered.
laws.penalty: First-degree stalking: felony. Second-degree: misdemeanor.
laws.exceptions: Lawful investigations by law enforcement are not considered stalking.

quiz.q: Is cyberstalking (electronic harassment) covered by Michigan's stalking law?
quiz.explanation: Michigan's stalking law covers cyberstalking through electronic means.

laws.title: Consumer Data Privacy Law
laws.subtitle: MCL §Privacy Act — Breach notification law
laws.fullDescription: Michigan: Data breach notification required.
laws.penalty: Data breach notification: civil fines.
laws.exceptions: Small businesses may have reduced obligations under some state laws.

quiz.q: Does Michigan have a comprehensive consumer data privacy law?
quiz.explanation: Michigan: Breach notification rules only.

laws.title: Social Media Age Verification
laws.subtitle: MCL §N/A — No state law
laws.fullDescription: Michigan: No social media age verification law.
laws.penalty: N/A — enforcement mechanisms vary.
laws.exceptions: Federal platforms regulation may preempt state laws.

quiz.q: Does Michigan require age verification for social media?
quiz.explanation: Michigan: No social media age verification law.

laws.title: Environmental Regulations
laws.subtitle: MCL §Environmental Code — Environmental protection
laws.fullDescription: Michigan: State env agency enforces air, water, waste rules.
laws.penalty: Environmental violations: civil fines up to $25000/day; criminal penalties for willful violations.
laws.exceptions: Some agricultural and industrial uses have specific permitting pathways.

quiz.q: Which agency enforces environmental laws in Michigan?
quiz.explanation: Michigan's state environmental agency works alongside the EPA to enforce environmental laws.

laws.title: Renewable Energy Standards
laws.subtitle: MCL §Energy Code — Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS)
laws.fullDescription: Michigan: Michigan has an RPS targeting 60% clean energy by 2035 and 100% carbon-neutral by 2040.
laws.penalty: N/A — this is a policy/utility requirement, not a criminal law.
laws.exceptions: Utilities that miss RPS targets may pay alternative compliance payments.

quiz.q: Does Michigan have a Renewable Portfolio Standard (RPS)?
quiz.explanation: Michigan: Michigan has aggressive clean energy targets: 100% carbon-neutral electricity by 2040.

laws.title: Plastic Bag Laws
laws.subtitle: MCL §N/A — No statewide law
laws.fullDescription: Michigan: No statewide plastic bag law.
laws.penalty: Retailer violations: N/A.
laws.exceptions: Bags for meat, produce, or bulk items are often exempt.

quiz.q: Does Michigan have a statewide plastic bag ban or fee?
quiz.explanation: Michigan: No statewide plastic bag law.

laws.title: Bottle Deposit Law
laws.subtitle: MCL §N/A — Bottle bill status
laws.fullDescription: Michigan: Michigan has a 10-cent bottle deposit — the highest in the US — covering most beverage containers.
laws.penalty: Retailers not accepting returns may face fines.
laws.exceptions: Some municipal redemption centers supplement mandatory deposit systems.

quiz.q: Does Michigan have a bottle deposit/redemption law?
quiz.explanation: Michigan: Michigan has a 10-cent bottle deposit — the highest in the US.

laws.title: Animal Cruelty Laws
laws.subtitle: MCL §Criminal Code — Animal cruelty prohibition
laws.fullDescription: Michigan prohibits cruelty to animals including torture, beating, neglect, and fighting. Animal cruelty is a felony; neglect is a misdemeanor.
laws.penalty: Intentional cruelty: felony (up to 5 years). Neglect: misdemeanor.
laws.exceptions: Lawful hunting, fishing, pest control, and veterinary procedures are exempt.

quiz.q: What is the maximum penalty for intentional animal cruelty in Michigan?
quiz.explanation: Michigan: Intentional animal cruelty is punishable by felony (up to 5 years).

laws.title: Exotic Pet Ownership
laws.subtitle: MCL §Wildlife Code — Exotic and wild animal ownership
laws.fullDescription: Michigan: Dangerous exotic animals generally prohibited as pets.
laws.penalty: Unlawful possession of prohibited animal: misdemeanor or felony; animal seizure..
laws.exceptions: Licensed zoos, wildlife rehabilitators, and research institutions may keep otherwise prohibited animals.

quiz.q: Are large exotic cats (lions, tigers) legal as pets in Michigan?
quiz.explanation: Michigan: Large exotic cats banned as pets.

laws.title: Fireworks Laws
laws.subtitle: MCL §Fire Safety Code — Consumer fireworks regulations
laws.fullDescription: Michigan: Consumer fireworks regulated.
laws.penalty: Fireworks violation: $500–$2000 fines plus liability for fire damage.
laws.exceptions: Licensed pyrotechnic operators may use professional-grade fireworks at permitted events.

quiz.q: Are consumer aerial fireworks legal in Michigan?
quiz.explanation: Michigan: Safe-and-sane fireworks allowed with local restrictions.

laws.title: Gambling Laws
laws.subtitle: MCL §Gaming Code — Gambling regulations
laws.fullDescription: Michigan: Michigan has commercial casinos in Detroit plus tribal casinos across the state. Online gaming and sports betting legalized 2019.
laws.penalty: Illegal gambling: Illegal gambling: misdemeanor..
laws.exceptions: Charitable gaming (bingo, pull tabs) for nonprofits typically permitted with license.

quiz.q: Are commercial casinos legal in Michigan?
quiz.explanation: Michigan: Michigan has commercial casinos, tribal gaming, and legal sports betting.

laws.title: Net Neutrality (State Level)
laws.subtitle: MCL §N/A — Internet regulation
laws.fullDescription: Michigan: No state net neutrality law.
laws.penalty: N/A — enforcement varies by state.
laws.exceptions: Federal FCC rules may preempt conflicting state laws.

quiz.q: Does Michigan have a state net neutrality law?
quiz.explanation: Michigan: No state net neutrality law.

laws.title: Right to Repair Laws
laws.subtitle: MCL §N/A — Consumer right to repair
laws.fullDescription: Michigan: No right-to-repair law.
laws.penalty: N/A — this defines consumer rights.
laws.exceptions: Some manufacturers have voluntarily expanded repair access independent of state laws.

quiz.q: Does Michigan have a right-to-repair law?
quiz.explanation: Michigan: No right-to-repair law.

laws.title: LGBTQ+ Employment Protections
laws.subtitle: MCL §Civil Rights Code — Sexual orientation and gender identity protections
laws.fullDescription: Michigan: Michigan does not explicitly list sexual orientation or gender identity in state civil rights law, though executive orders and court rulings provide some protections. Bills to add explicit protections have been introduced.
laws.penalty: Employment discrimination based on LGBTQ+ status: same remedies as other protected classes.
laws.exceptions: The federal Bostock v. Clayton County (2020) ruling extended Title VII to cover LGBTQ+ workers nationwide.

quiz.q: Are LGBTQ+ workers explicitly protected by Michigan state law?
quiz.explanation: Michigan: Michigan does not explicitly protect LGBTQ+ workers under state civil rights law.
